svg.title: The Binance book before a top-taker fire, a look-alike our model scores the same, and an ordinary moment
svg.desc: Three columns of three panels: best-level sizes, aggressive trades and the Binance mid change, from -1000 to +300 ms around each moment.
svg.text: Same picture, no fire: the top taker's fire and the two ordinary moments most like it
Binance futures best level, 1 s before to 0.3 s after (t = 0: the fire's order reaching Predict). Look-alikes: nearest on nine key book inputs, same day, same bet (up).
Far side (must empty for the price to move their way); trades hitting it
Typical fire: the top taker's order
far 1.33 · near 11.11 BTC · moved their way +6 ms
Best-level size, BTC (log scale; under 0.1 drawn at 0.1)
far 1.80 · near 12.72 BTC · no move in 300 ms
far 0.81 · near 10.64 BTC · no move in 300 ms
For each of its 4,424 fires, the 20 ordinary moments most like it moved their way within 300 ms 5.8% of the time (the closest 8.1%); its fires 61%.
The closest fifth of look-alikes moved 3.1%. A fire's closest ordinary look-alike sits nearer to it (median distance 0.71) than its closest other fire (0.96).
Our model already rates these pictures high (fires 7.2%, look-alikes 5.5%, random 2.5%); what it cannot see is which of them will move.
The fire's busier last second is in our other inputs (1 s / 5 s activity): over all 298, the fire look predicts moves at AUC 0.50 (SIGNAL_VS_NOISE).
Four consumed days; development evidence. The look-alikes are taken whatever their outcome.
